objective: Make release announcements fire without a human, and never announce a red release. bot/bot.py line 305 calls publish_release_announcement() exactly once from setup_hook, so an announcement can only happen when an operator restarts the bot — the release half of the mission's feedback loop is manual. Turn that one-shot into a periodic loop with the same shape as publish_weekly_digests (which already polls in this file), and gate it: the resolved range-end SHA must be green in CI before the range is reserved. The at-most-once machinery makes repetition safe already — release_announce dedups on range_end and INSERT OR IGNORE reserves before sending — so a cycle that finds nothing new does nothing. Two PM rulings are binding here and are not the executor's to revisit: poll every 300s (env-overridable, floored at 60s), and treat unknown CI status as not-green so nothing is announced. Announcing late is cheap; announcing a red release is not, and issue 158 shows a red commit can reach main.
constraints: ORDERING IS THE WHOLE POINT: resolve the range end, then check that SHA is green, and only then run the INSERT OR IGNORE reservation. A SHA that gets reserved and then rejected as red is permanently un-announceable, because range_end is the dedup key. A test must pin this by asserting the release_announce row count is unchanged after a not-green cycle.

publish_release_announcement becomes `await self.wait_until_ready()` then `while not self.is_closed():` with the announce call wrapped in try/except printing the error, then `await asyncio.sleep(interval)` — structurally identical to publish_weekly_digests. Do not invent a scheduler, a discord.ext.tasks dependency, or a backoff policy.

Interval: read RELEASE_ANNOUNCE_POLL_SECONDS, default 300, floor 60 (a smaller value is raised to 60, not rejected). A non-numeric value falls back to 300 with a printed reason rather than crashing the loop.

Green detection reads GitHub for the resolved SHA using the requests/GH_API/GITHUB_TOKEN pattern already in this file, in a helper that is a plain function so tests can patch it. Green means: at least one completed check-run or commit status for that SHA, every one of them concluded success/neutral/skipped, and none are queued/in_progress/pending. Anything else — including zero checks — is not green.

FAIL CLOSED. Unset GITHUB_REPO or GITHUB_TOKEN, a non-2xx response, a timeout, a request exception, or an unparseable body all mean not green: print one line naming the reason and return False. Never announce on an assumption. This is I5's posture (honest under uncertainty) applied to the release loop.
Network calls in the loop go through asyncio.to_thread like the existing resolve_release_ref and collect_release calls; do not block the event loop, and set an explicit request timeout.

The green gate is unconditional — there is no env flag to disable it. If a green check ever becomes the thing blocking a release, that is a PM decision to revisit, not a runtime toggle for an operator to flip under pressure.
A not-green tip is not an error and must not spam: print at most one line per cycle, and do not raise.

Existing tests in tests/test_announce.py may be EXTENDED, and existing cases may be edited ONLY to stub the new green check so they exercise the green path. Their existing assertions — scrubbing, at-most-once, empty-range marker, send-failure reservation, composer capping — stay exactly as they are. No test is deleted, skipped, or weakened; the issue carries test-change-authorized for exactly this narrow edit.

Do not touch relay_decisions, publish_weekly_digests, on_message, /suggest, the nudge cache, or compose_release_announcement's content. The overlay copy is TASK-300-S4's job and merging the two makes both harder to review.
Branch backend/TASK-300-S3-<slug>. A literal role/... branch is refused by completion proof #4.

Issue 163 is a STAGE issue and closing it is correct: write 'Fixes #163' exactly once in the PR body. Do not write a bare '#163' anywhere else, and never write a bare '#97' or '#164' in any commit message or PR body — refer to them as 'issue 97' and 'issue 164'. Four accidental parent closures happened on 2026-08-04 from exactly this pattern. Check before pushing: `gh pr view <n> --json body -q .body | grep -c '#97'` must be 0.
forbidden_actions: Reserving a range (INSERT OR IGNORE into release_announce) before the range end is confirmed green
Adding an env var, flag or code path that disables or bypasses the green gate
Treating an unknown, errored, missing or in-progress CI status as green
Deleting, skipping or loosening any existing assertion in tests/test_announce.py
Editing bot/release_notes.py, bot/digest.py, or anything under .github/
Changing announcement copy or the compose/scrub pipeline (that is TASK-300-S4)
required_checks: python3 -m pytest tests/test_announce.py tests/test_bot.py tests/test_digest.py bot/tests/test_release_notes.py -q

acceptance_criteria.text: publish_release_announcement awaits readiness then loops until the client is closed, catching and printing per-iteration exceptions and sleeping the configured interval between cycles, in the same shape as publish_weekly_digests.

The interval is RELEASE_ANNOUNCE_POLL_SECONDS, default 300, floored at 60, with a non-numeric value falling back to 300 and printing a reason; a test asserts the default, the override, the floor and the fallback.
A test drives several loop iterations — including one where announce_release_once raises — and asserts the loop keeps running and the sleep interval is honored.

announce_release_once resolves the range end, verifies that SHA is green, and returns False WITHOUT inserting any row when it is not; the test asserts the release_announce row count is identical before and after.

Green detection is fail-closed for every failure mode: unset GITHUB_REPO or GITHUB_TOKEN, non-2xx, request exception, queued/in_progress checks, any non-success conclusion, and zero checks each yield not-green with a one-line printed reason; each is covered by a test case.

On a green SHA the existing behavior is unchanged: reserve, send exactly once, set posted_at, never repost the same range_end — proven by the pre-existing test_announce cases still passing with only a green stub added.

A red tip followed by a later green tip announces the range ending at the green SHA with range_start still the prior range_end, so no merged commit is skipped; asserted by a test over a red-then-green sequence.

bot/README.md documents the periodic loop, RELEASE_ANNOUNCE_POLL_SECONDS, the green gate and its fail-closed posture, and the standing operator requirement that RELEASE_SINCE_REF be set in the bot runtime for the first announcement.

Both required checks pass; no test is deleted or skipped; bot/release_notes.py, bot/digest.py, tests/test_bot.py and tests/test_digest.py are byte-identical to main; relay_decisions, publish_weekly_digests, on_message and /suggest are unmodified.

rollback: Revert the branch: announcements go back to firing once per operator restart, and nothing is mis-announced in the meantime. Safe to revert alone — TASK-300-S4 depends on this stage's file state but not on its behavior, so a revert after S4 lands would leave the overlay headline correct but again human-triggered.
